title: Cold Chain Delivery Receipt Form
subtitle: Reconcile the promised cold chain delivery with actual units, condition, custody, evidence, exceptions, receiving decision, and accountable handoff.
description: An original, fillable cold chain delivery receipt form for controlling temperature-controlled consignment and product-integrity record through delivery receipt identity, observations, evidence, decision, exceptions, escalation, completion, handoff, and final verification without replacing applicable requirements or professional review.
use_case: Use at Approved receiving and quarantine location when authorized temperature-controlled receiving location and the delivering custodian need one receipt that separates physical handoff from inspection, hold, commercial acceptance, and exception resolution.

sections.title: Cold Chain delivery receipt identity and routing
sections.guidance: Anchor the record to the exact work, parties, locations, and source references.

fields.label: Shipment, order, lane, and protocol reference
Lot, pallet, shipper, logger, sensor, or seal ID

blocks.label: Responsible parties and route points

fields.label: Trained Cold-Chain Shipper, Carrier, And Receiver
Qualified storage, pack-out, and loading location

blocks.guidance: Preserve linkage to the shipping protocol, product requirements, lane plan, and logger instructions.

sections.title: Cold Chain delivery commitment and receiving readiness
sections.guidance: Confirm what was expected, where it was due, and which controls governed acceptance.

fields.label: Approved range, excursion, sanitation, and product-release control

blocks.label: Cold Chain delivery and receiving controls
items: Maintain approved chilled range
Maintain approved frozen range
Protect from freezing
Qualified passive shipper
Active refrigerated equipment
Continuous logger or sensor monitoring
Minimize door-open and staging exposure
Quarantine on alarm, missing data, or uncertain control
blocks.guidance: Confirm applicable controls before unloading, opening, moving, or accepting the delivered units.

sections.title: Cold Chain delivered-unit reconciliation
sections.guidance: Reconcile each delivered identity and quantity before relying on totals or signatures.

blocks.label: Cold-Chain Lots, Shippers, Pallets, Sensors, Seals, And Controlled Quantities received

columns.label: Lot, pallet, shipper, logger, sensor, or seal ID
Product, shipper, coolant, seal, and logger condition
Approved range, excursion, sanitation, and product-release control

blocks.label: Receipt totals and reconciliation
blocks.guidance: Shipped, monitored, received, and disposition quantity

sections.title: Cold Chain condition inspection and receipt evidence
sections.guidance: Preserve observations made before the receiver changes packaging, custody, or physical condition.

blocks.label: Cold Chain receipt inspection
items: Shipment, product, lot, quantity, lane, and approved temperature range agree
Packaging configuration and coolant match the approved shipping protocol
Coolant conditioning and pack-out timing are within the defined work instruction
Logger or sensor identity, calibration status, battery, placement, and start are verified
Vehicle or compartment is clean, compatible, and preconditioned where required
Seal, shipper, pallet, and tamper condition are documented at each custody point
Door-open time, staging exposure, delays, and power interruptions are recorded
Arrival product, ambient, display, and logger status support an initial assessment
Alarm, excursion, missing data, damage, or contamination triggers quarantine
Only a qualified reviewer may authorize product disposition under applicable requirements

blocks.label: Receipt evidence index
blocks.guidance: Record only necessary proof and preserve privacy or security restrictions.

blocks.label: Condition, count, custody, and acceptance narrative

fields.label: Condition, count, custody, and acceptance narrative

blocks.guidance: Describe facts that cannot be reconstructed from the line table or evidence reference.

sections.title: Cold Chain exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, affected scope, immediate control, owner, deadline, and escalation reconstructable.

blocks.label: Cold Chain exception indicators
items: Product, lot, quantity, range, route, or protocol mismatch
Packaging or coolant configuration differs from the approved pack-out
Logger missing, expired, uncalibrated, failed, stopped, or incorrectly placed
Vehicle or container not clean, compatible, or adequately preconditioned
Seal damage, shipper damage, leakage, contamination, or tampering
Temperature alarm, excursion, freeze event, or missing data interval
Delay, door-open exposure, power interruption, or unplanned transfer
Receiving site cannot maintain quarantine or controlled storage
Product released, moved, sold, or used before qualified disposition
Custody, timing, or evidence cannot reconstruct the exposure history
blocks.guidance: Select every observed condition; do not use a generic exception mark when the actual trigger is known.

blocks.label: Receipt hold, partial acceptance, refusal, or resolution

sections.title: Cold Chain receipt decision and custody transfer
sections.guidance: Separate physical custody from final commercial, quality, safety, or financial acceptance.

blocks.label: Delivery and receiving attestation
blocks.guidance: Attestation confirms the recorded physical event, not waiver of a concealed issue or unresolved review.

sections.title: Cold Chain delivery receipt closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: This cold chain delivery receipt is an operational record, not a substitute for applicable law, contract terms, safety or product requirements, or professional judgment. Stop the affected movement, transfer, release, posting, or disposition when identity, evidence, authorization, or control is uncertain. A qualified qualified quality, food-safety, pharmacy, or product-integrity reviewer must review the exception and document the controlling decision.

blocks.label: Prepared, reviewed, and accepted

fields.label: Reviewed by qualified quality, food-safety, pharmacy, or product-integrity reviewer

blocks.guidance: A signature records accountability for the stated decision; it does not cure missing evidence or override a stop condition.
